entries.subject: VLTI/PIONIER September 2014 H-band visibilities, JMMC OiDB
entries.finding: The image-ready calibrated file of Paladini et al. (2018) is public in the OiDB at calibration level 3 (data PI C. Paladini): 303 squared-visibility and 201 closure-phase rows in three H-band channels over the nights of 25, 26, 29 and 30 September 2014, longest projected baseline 82.3 m, no channel flagged. A uniform disc of 18.17 mas fits the squared visibilities at reduced chi-squared 51: the data demand structure on the disc.

entries.subject: Image reconstruction with SQUEEZE versus the published image
entries.finding: The public SQUEEZE code at the commit pinned for Betelgeuse, with the same prior and hyperparameter (maximum entropy, multiplier 10, uniform-disc start, 0.4 mas pixels), fits the file at reduced chi-squared 2.45 on squared visibilities and 1.06 on closure phases and shows a disc of a few large bright cells, the pattern the paper reports. The independent transform in reconstruction.test.mts agrees. The published image itself is not redistributed here.

entries.subject: Rotation axis, period and prime meridian
entries.finding: No publication measures the rotation axis or period of π¹ Gruis. The object uses the display-orientation record: the axis shown is celestial north in the plane of the sky and the display meridian faces the Earth at the scene epoch, both labelled as a convention in the lens notes and the README.
entries.revisitWhen: A measured position angle of the rotation axis, as ALMA gave for Betelgeuse, is published.

entries.subject: Catalogued radial velocity for the placement
entries.finding: SIMBAD lists no radial velocity and the Pulkovo, GCRV and Kharchenko compilations have no entry for HIP 110478. The star record assumes zero; over the 26 years since J2000 a 30 km/s error moves the scene position by one part in a million of the distance.
entries.revisitWhen: A catalogued heliocentric radial velocity with a bibcode is found.
